body:
**Another data point: this reproduces outside Godot, and there is a workaround that keeps exclusive fullscreen.**

I ran into this in **Minecraft: Java Edition** (LWJGL, OpenGL) on hardware close to one of the configs already in this thread.

### System

- NVIDIA RTX 5080, driver **32.0.16.1088** (2026-07-22) — newer than the 32.0.15.7688 in the report, still affected
- Windows 11 Pro **10.0.26200** (Build 26200)
- AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D
- 3 displays, primary 2560x1440

### Measurements

Sampled every 2 s from Windows performance counters (`\GPU Adapter Memory(*)\Dedicated Usage` and `\GPU Process Memory(*)\Dedicated Usage` / `Shared Usage`), filtered to the game process:

| State | Dedicated VRAM |
|---|---|
| Windowed, idle, 150 s | flat at **1185 MB**, zero growth across 50 consecutive samples |
| Exclusive fullscreen, idle, 82 s | **1707 → 13472 MB** (~226 MB/s), hits the dedicated ceiling, then spills into shared memory up to **3168 MB** |
| Leaving fullscreen | **13464 → 628 MB** within a single 2 s sample |

Nothing accumulates across cycles — usage returns to baseline (or slightly below) every time, and stays flat for minutes afterwards in windowed mode.

**The player character was completely stationary for the entire fullscreen test.** No movement, no camera motion, no terrain streaming, no particle-heavy events. This may be worth noting, since the original report associates the leak with animations triggering CPU particles — here there is effectively no workload and it still climbs at the full rate. That suggests the allocation is tied to presentation, not to rendering work.

### Workaround that does not require giving up exclusive fullscreen

**NVIDIA Control Panel → Manage 3D Settings → "Vulkan/OpenGL present method" → "Prefer layered on DXGI Swapchain"**

This eliminated the leak entirely for me while staying in exclusive fullscreen. Confirmed both with and without an OpenGL shader pipeline (Iris shaders, a substantially heavier GL load).

I could not find this mentioned anywhere in the thread. If it holds up for others it is a more convenient mitigation than switching to `WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN`, and it may also narrow down where the leak lives, since it moves presentation off the native OpenGL path and onto a DXGI swapchain.

### Ruled out on my side

Before landing on the driver, I eliminated the following by measurement, in case it saves anyone time: the chunk renderer mod (Sodium vs Embeddium), the shader mod (Iris — the leak persists with it fully removed, and does not occur in another pack that has it installed), render distance, and VSync. The behaviour is below all of them.
